sources.title: Planning obligations
sources.verified_claim: Enfield states CIL and Section 106 are used to mitigate development impacts and fund infrastructure; CIL generally applies to qualifying development and S106 is site-specific, with permission granted only after the agreement is signed where required.

sources.title: Section 106 planning obligations
sources.verified_claim: Havering states S106 agreements are legally binding and are assessed case by case to offset or mitigate development impacts; existence of the framework does not establish an obligation for the sample parcel.

sources.title: Havering Community Infrastructure Levy
sources.verified_claim: Havering states its CIL applies to CIL-liable developments granted permission from 1 September 2019 and that Mayoral CIL may also apply; site payment status requires separate enquiry.

sources.title: Developer contributions
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth defines CIL and S106 as mechanisms for financial and non-financial contributions, including affordable housing and infrastructure, to support development and mitigate impacts.

sources.title: Section 106 planning obligations
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states S106 agreements bind land and may secure affordable housing, workspace, carbon limits or other mitigation; obligations must be necessary, directly related, and proportionate to the development.

sources.title: Guidance for submitting details relating to a section 106 agreement
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth lists implementation, practical completion, occupation and other triggers that may require notices or details under S106 agreements, showing obligations continue through delivery stages.

sources.title: Fees and charges
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth provides a formal route to obtain S106 deeds and compliance letters; this enables site-specific verification later but does not establish current compliance for the sample parcel.

sources.title: Time-limited relief from the Community Infrastructure Levy in London
sources.verified_claim: Government opened consultation on proposed time-limited borough-level CIL relief for qualifying Greater London developments and corrected the draft instrument on 17 July 2026; the proposal remains consultation, not adopted relief.
